mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals increased demand in the housing market, leading to positive economic growth expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increases over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows an annualized growth rate below 1%, it signals a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL annualized growth < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals strong job growth, leading to increased consumer confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% annually and GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 2% annually, it signals a potential mismatch between consumer spending and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annual growth > 5% and GDPC1 annual growth < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances where RSAFS annual growth > 5% and GDPC1 annual growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25pp in a month.
